label: History
value: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables
unit: Anne Shirley arrives at Green Gables in Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, after siblings Matthew and Marilla Cuthbert decide to adopt an orphan boy but receive Anne by mistake. Though Marilla initially intends to send her back, Matthew's quiet fondness and Anne's passionate plea convince them to keep her. Anne grows up in Avonlea, making a soulmate friendship with Diana Barry, causing various humorous and disastrous scrapes due to her vivid imagination, and developing a fierce academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe after he calls her 'Carrots.' She attends Queen's Academy, earning her teacher's license and winning the Avery Scholarship. Following Matthew's sudden death from a heart attack and Marilla's failing eyesight, Anne waives her scholarship to stay at Green Gables, taking a local teaching job in Avonlea to support Marilla and help raise the orphaned Keith twins, Davy and Dora. During two years of teaching, she helps organize the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and reconciles her long-standing grudge against Gilbert, becoming close friends with him. Later, supported by an inheritance from Miss Josephine Barry, Anne attends Redmond College in Kingsport, earning her B.A. with High Honors in English. During her college years she lives at Patty's Place with her friends, receives and rejects a proposal from the handsome, wealthy Roy Gardner upon realizing she does not truly love him, and eventually realizes her deep, enduring love for Gilbert Blythe, accepting his proposal of marriage after he recovers from a dangerous bout of typhoid fever.

label: History
value: Anthony Pye came to Avonlea as an orphan
unit: Anthony Pye came to Avonlea as an orphan to live with his aunt and uncle, Mr. and Mrs. George Pye, and entered the Avonlea school under Anne Shirley. Holding a firm belief that girl teachers were useless, he treated Anne with open scorn and disdained her attempts to win him over with kindness. During Anne's first year of teaching, he engaged in various acts of mischief, such as pouring water down a classmate's neck and putting a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer. After he insolently confessed to the mouse prank, an exasperated Anne lost her temper and whipped him with her pointer. To Anne's surprise, this punishment earned her his respect, as he considered it 'just as good as a man's.' From that point on, Anthony's attitude toward Anne improved significantly; he began carrying her books to school and acknowledged that she was 'some good after all.' When Anne resigned her post two years later, Anthony was deeply upset by the news and fought two battles with other boys to vent his feelings.

Holding a firm belief that girl teachers were useless, he treated Anne with open scorn and disdained her attempts to win him over with kindness. During Anne's first year of teaching, he engaged in various acts of mischief, such as pouring water down a classmate's neck and putting a live mouse in Anne's desk drawer. After he insolently confessed to the mouse prank, an exasperated Anne lost her temper and whipped him with her pointer. To Anne's surprise, this punishment earned her his respect, as he considered it 'just as good as a man's.' From that point on, Anthony's attitude toward Anne improved significantly; he began carrying her books to school and acknowledged that she was 'some good after all.' When Anne resigned her post two years later, Anthony was deeply upset by the news and fought two battles with other boys to vent his feelings.

value: Aunt Jamesina possesses a bright spirit.
unit: Aunt Jamesina possesses a bright, cheerful, and youthful spirit that belie her years, believing in indulging herself in old-fashioned opinions and comfortable ways. She has an active sense of humor, a soft heart, and an open, indulgent attitude toward young people. Though devout and respectful of religious duties, she is tolerant and prefers to let the girls manage their own affairs rather than scold or supervise them strictly. She is also an animal lover who refuses to abandon stray cats.

label: History
value: Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house after her daughter married and left for foreign mission work.
unit: After her daughter married and left for foreign mission work, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house until her niece, Stella Maynard, invited her to keep house for a group of Redmond students at Patty's Place in Kingsport. She accepted and took along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph. At Patty's Place, she presided over the household with gentle humor and warm-heartedness, accommodating Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon. She also took in Rusty, a stray cat that Anne rescued, and insisted on staying at Patty's Place over the Christmas holidays rather than leave the animals alone. At the end of the girls' college years, she decided to take all three cats to live with her at Green Gables to keep Marilla Cuthbert company when Anne left for her teaching position.

unit: After her daughter married and left for foreign mission work, Aunt Jamesina was left alone in a large house until her niece, Stella Maynard, invited her to keep house for a group of Redmond students at Patty's Place in Kingsport. She accepted and took along her two cats, the Sarah-cat and Joseph. At Patty's Place, she presided over the household with gentle humor and warm-heartedness, accommodating Anne Shirley, Priscilla Grant, Stella Maynard, and Philippa Gordon. She also took in Rusty, a stray cat that Anne rescued, and insisted on staying at Patty's Place over the Christmas holidays rather than leave the animals alone. At the end of the girls' college years, she decided to take all three cats to live with her at Green Gables to keep Marilla Cuthbert company when Anne left for her teaching position.

label: History
value: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Billy Andrews grew up in Avonlea and attended the local school. As a young man of twenty, he drove Anne, Diana, and his sister Jane to the White Sands Hotel concert, secretly admiring Anne despite his inability to converse with her. When his father deeded the upper farm to him, Billy wished to marry Anne but was too shy to propose himself. He persuaded his sister Jane to propose on his behalf, offering to wait until Anne finished college if necessary. After Anne declined, Billy turned his attentions to Nettie Blewett, whom he married the following June. The couple 'appeared out' at Avonlea church shortly after their wedding before moving into their new home.

unit: Leonora Bowman became the fourth of her sisters to serve as Miss Lavendar Lewis's maid at Echo Lodge when she was thirteen years old, taking on the customary household name of 'Charlotta the Fourth.' When Anne Shirley and Diana Barry accidentally stumbled upon Echo Lodge, Charlotta welcomed them and assisted in entertaining the guests. She formed a deep admiration for Anne, secretly trying to imitate her manners and posture. She served as a faithful helper during the reunion and courtship of Miss Lavendar and Stephen Irving, anxiously helping with wedding preparations. Following Miss Lavendar's marriage to Mr. Irving, Charlotta accompanied them to Boston to continue living with them.

value: > You're awful nice, Anne. Milty Boulter wrote on his slate today and showed it to Jennie Sloane, 'Roses red and vi'lets blue, Sugar's sweet, and so are you' and that 'spresses my feelings for you ezackly, Anne.

value: > Anne, don't you like me a little bit, even if I ain't a good boy like Paul?

value: > I'm going to be gooder, and I'll tell you how I know it. Today Marilla give me two pieces of bread and jam, one for me and one for Dora. One was a good deal bigger than the other and Marilla didn't say which was mine. But I give the biggest piece to Dora. That was good of me, wasn't it?

label: History
value: Davy Keith and Dora are twins.
unit: Davy Keith and his twin sister, Dora, were left orphans at the age of six when their mother, Mary Keith, died of a lingering illness in East Grafton. Because their uncle in British Columbia could not immediately care for them, Marilla Cuthbert took the twins into Green Gables. Davy quickly established a reputation for endless antics, such as dropping a caterpillar down a girl's neck in church, trapping his sister Dora in a toolhouse, putting a toad in Marilla's bed, and chasing Mrs. Lynde's rooster to death. Despite his frequent misbehavior and knack for telling wild stories, Anne Shirley took a gentle approach to his discipline, earning his deep devotion and gradually helping him learn right from wrong. Following the death of his uncle Richard, who left a trust fund for the twins, Davy and Dora became permanent residents of Green Gables. As he grew older, Davy attended Avonlea school, befriended boys like Milty Boulter, and slowly matured into a handsome, albeit still lively and inquisitive, schoolboy.

They spent their childhood exploring the nearby woods and fields, founding a Story Club, and sharing their secrets. Diana attended Avonlea school alongside Anne and participated in local events, including the Avonlea Debating Club concert. After accidentally becoming intoxicated on Marilla's currant wine during a tea party, she was temporarily forbidden by her mother from playing with Anne, but they were reconciled after Anne saved Diana's younger sister Minnie May during a severe attack of croup. In their late teens, Diana joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and helped canvass the community for local causes. Though she did not attend college like Anne, she remained her most loyal companion in Avonlea. She eventually fell in love with Fred Wright, and the two became engaged and married in an old-fashioned summer ceremony at Orchard Slope. The couple settled on a farm in Avonlea, where Diana gave birth to her first child, a son named Fred.

label: History
value: Dora Keith is the daughter of Mary Keith
unit: Dora Keith was born the daughter of Mary Keith and a third cousin of Marilla Cuthbert. After her father died in her infancy and her mother succumbed to a long illness, she and her twin brother Davy were taken in by Marilla Cuthbert and Anne Shirley at Green Gables. Unlike her mischievous brother, Dora quickly settled into life at Green Gables, exhibiting quiet, orderly habits and a desire to help with household tasks. She began attending Avonlea School under Anne's instruction when she turned seven. When her uncle Richard died in British Columbia, he left a trust fund for her and Davy, securing their permanent home at Green Gables under Marilla's care.

label: History
value: Gilbert grew up in Avonlea
unit: Gilbert grew up in Avonlea but spent three years in Alberta with his father before returning to Avonlea School at age fourteen. On his first afternoon back, he jokingly pulled Anne Shirley's red braid and called her 'Carrots,' prompting her to smash a slate over his head. Though he immediately apologized, Anne nursed a grudge for years, ignoring his repeated attempts at reconciliation, including rescuing her when her dory sank during a play of 'Elaine.' Gilbert competed fiercely with Anne for top honors at school and Queen's Academy, where both graduated into the fifth class and eventually tied for first place on the Entrance Examinations. Upon graduating from Queen's, Gilbert voluntarily gave up his appointment as teacher of the Avonlea school so that Anne could remain at Green Gables with Marilla after Matthew's death, accepting the White Sands school instead. He later attended Redmond College, becoming Freshman Class President, captain of the football team, and winner of the prestigious Cooper Prize in Classics. During his Junior year, he proposed to Anne at Patty's Place but was refused, leading to a period of distant friendship. Following graduation, Gilbert fell dangerously ill with typhoid fever in Avonlea, but recovered, after which he reconciled with Anne during a walk to Hester Gray's garden, where she accepted his proposal of marriage.

label: History
value: Mr. Harrison's sister died in Scottsford, New Brunswick.
unit: After the death of his sister in Scottsford, New Brunswick, Mr. Harrison married Emily Scott, a immaculate housekeeper. Their stark differences in domestic habits—especially regarding her excessive neatness and his swearing parrot, Ginger—led to a bitter separation. Leaving his wife behind, Mr. Harrison moved to Avonlea, Prince Edward Island, where he bought Robert Bell's farm next door to Green Gables and lived as a supposed bachelor. Initially gaining a reputation as an eccentric and irritable crank, he clashed with Anne Shirley after her Jersey cow trampled his oatfield, but the two quickly reconciled and became warm friends over tea and cake. He supported the Avonlea Village Improvement Society in his own gruff manner and offered Anne humorously frank advice on her writing and teaching. During a severe hail-and-thunder storm his house was struck by lightning and his beloved parrot Ginger was killed. Shortly thereafter, his wife Emily arrived at his farm, having discovered his whereabouts through a joke item in a Charlottetown newspaper; the couple reconciled and happily resumed their marriage. Following her arrival, Mr. Harrison became a tidy, well-shaved, church-going citizen of Avonlea, while maintaining his friendship with Anne and his unique, blunt outlook on life.

label: History
value: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea
unit: Jane Andrews grew up in Avonlea as a classmate and close friend of Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis. She attended Queen's Academy alongside Anne, earning her teacher's license and excelling in domestic science. After graduating, she taught at the Newbridge school for two years. She later went West to teach, eventually taking a school in Winnipeg. While in the West, she met Edward Inglis, a wealthy English Winnipeg millionaire, and became engaged to him. Before leaving for her new life, she served as a matchmaker by proposing to Anne on behalf of her shy brother, Billy Andrews, though Anne declined the offer. Jane subsequently married Mr. Inglis in a lavish ceremony at her home in Avonlea and departed on a wedding tour to Europe.

label: History
value: Josie Pye attends Avonlea School
unit: Josie Pye attends Avonlea School alongside Anne Shirley and her peers. She earns a reputation among her classmates as a cheat and a spiteful girl. During a party at the Barry home, Josie dares Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's roof, which leads to Anne falling and breaking her ankle. Later, Josie joins the Queen's Academy preparation class and passes the entrance examinations. After attending Queen's, she continues her studies at Redmond College alongside Anne and their friends. During their time at Redmond, she frequently makes barbed and envious comments toward Anne, such as accusing her of copying her prize-winning story.

label: History
value: Lavendar Lewis spent twenty-five years living a retired life at Echo Lodge in Grafton.
unit: Miss Lavendar Lewis spent twenty-five years living a retired life at Echo Lodge in Grafton after a youthful engagement with Stephen Irving was broken due to a foolish quarrel and her own stubborn pride. To combat her loneliness, she created an imaginary world, pretending to host tea parties and imagining a little dream-boy as her child. Anne Shirley and Diana Barry discovered her house by accident while lost, and Anne instantly recognized her as a kindred spirit. Anne later brought Stephen's son, Paul Irving, to meet her. Realizing Stephen was back in Prince Edward Island, Anne arranged a meeting between the former lovers. Stephen visited Miss Lavendar at Echo Lodge, and they reconciled after twenty-five years apart. They were married in the garden under the honeysuckle trellis the following August, subsequently leaving for a wedding trip to the Pacific coast before moving to Boston with Paul and Charlotta the Fourth.

label: History
value: Marilla Cuthbert decides to adopt an orphan boy.
unit: Marilla Cuthbert and her brother Matthew decide to adopt an orphan boy to assist with farmwork at Green Gables. Due to a misunderstanding, an eleven-year-old girl named Anne Shirley is delivered instead. Though Marilla initially intends to send Anne back, she relents after seeing the child's distress and deciding it is her duty to raise her. Over the next several years, Marilla strictly instructs Anne in household chores, morals, and decorum, gradually softening as she grows deeply attached to the girl's spirited personality. When Matthew dies suddenly of a heart attack following a bank failure, Marilla's grief is compound by a specialist's diagnosis that her failing eyesight will lead to blindness if she continues reading or sewing. Unable to manage the farm alone, Marilla prepares to sell Green Gables until Anne gives up her college scholarship to stay in Avonlea and teach. Marilla accepts a proposal for Mrs. Rachel Lynde to move into Green Gables, allowing Anne to attend Redmond College while ensuring Marilla has companionship and assistance in raising her orphan relatives, the twins Davy and Dora.

label: History
value: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea
unit: Paul Irving arrives in Avonlea from the United States at the age of ten to live with his grandmother, Mrs. Irving, following the death of his mother. He becomes a student at Avonlea school under Anne Shirley, with whom he instantly bonds as a kindred spirit over their shared love of imaginative concepts. He creates an intricate world of imaginary 'rock people' who live down by the shore, writing essays and stories about them. During his time in Avonlea, he also forms a close friendship with Miss Lavendar Lewis at Echo Lodge, whom he visits frequently. His father, Stephen Irving, returns to Avonlea and eventually reconciles with and marries Miss Lavendar. Following the wedding, Paul moves to Boston with his father, stepmother, and Charlotta the Fourth, though he continues to return to Avonlea and Echo Lodge for summer vacations.

value: Phil is gay
unit: Phil is gay, irrepressible, and intensely frivolous on the surface, but possesses a deep, loyal, and womanly nature underneath. She suffers from a comical degree of indecision when choosing between small options, often relying on hatpins or chance to make up her mind. Despite her aristocratic background and wealth, she is entirely free from snobbishness and genuinely affectionate toward her friends. She delights in being popular and surrounded by admirers, yet she is honest, generous, and ungrudging of others' good fortune.

value: Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley
unit: Philippa Gordon first met Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant in Old St. John's Cemetery during their freshman year at Redmond College. Finding herself instantly drawn to them, she introduced them into her wide social circle and became a close friend. The following year, she joined Anne, Priscilla, and Stella Maynard in renting Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, where she lived happily under the care of Aunt Jamesina. Although pursued by numerous admirers, including her hometown suitors Alec and Alonzo, Phil eventually fell deeply in love with Jonas Blake, a poor divinity student. Overcoming her initial reluctance to marry a poor man, she accepted his proposal during her junior year and stood firm against her mother's objections. After completing her Arts course and taking High Honors in Mathematics at Redmond, Philippa married Jonas in Bolingbroke with Anne as her bridesmaid.

value: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school.
unit: Mr. Phillips served as the schoolmaster at Avonlea school. During his tenure, he spent much of his time sitting at the back of the room explaining Latin lessons to Prissy Andrews, whom he courted. He was known for maintaining scandalous order and frequently using sarcastic punishments, such as forcing Anne Shirley to stand on the platform under a blackboard legend criticizing her temper or making her sit beside Gilbert Blythe as a punishment for tardiness. He also took part in local events, giving a recitation of Mark Antony's oration at the Avonlea Debating Club concert and presenting Mayflowers to Prissy Andrews during a field afternoon. At the end of June, he resigned his position as teacher, making a tearful farewell speech to his pupils before leaving Avonlea.

label: History
value: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy
unit: Priscilla Grant attended Queen's Academy with Anne Shirley and later taught at the Carmody school for two years. After deciding to further her education, she accepted the Carmody school position for another term before entering Redmond College. In her Freshman year at Redmond, she boarded at the same house as Anne Shirley and became a close friend and companion. Along with Anne, Philippa Gordon, and Stella Maynard, she helped set up house at Patty's Place under the chaperonage of Aunt Jamesina. Priscilla pursued a course in Classics, ultimately graduating from Redmond College with Honors in Classics.

label: History
value: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea
unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for many years at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea, diligently managing her home, church auxiliaries, and the Sewing Circle while keeping close watch over her neighbors. When the Cuthberts decided to adopt an orphan, she openly disapproved of the risky venture and later insulted young Anne Shirley's looks, prompting a fiery outburst from the girl. After Anne apologized, Mrs. Rachel quickly forgave her and grew to like her, eventually becoming a strong advocate for Anne's education and career. Over the years, Mrs. Rachel actively participated in local events, including the church bazaar and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society's efforts. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she nursed him devotedly until his death. Facing the necessity of selling her mortgaged farm, she accepted Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables, where she set up her quarters in the former spare room and helped care for the Keith twins.

unit: Mrs. Rachel Lynde lived for many years at Lynde's Hollow in Avonlea, diligently managing her home, church auxiliaries, and the Sewing Circle while keeping close watch over her neighbors. When the Cuthberts decided to adopt an orphan, she openly disapproved of the risky venture and later insulted young Anne Shirley's looks, prompting a fiery outburst from the girl. After Anne apologized, Mrs. Rachel quickly forgave her and grew to like her, eventually becoming a strong advocate for Anne's education and career. Over the years, Mrs. Rachel actively participated in local events, including the church bazaar and the Avonlea Village Improvement Society's efforts. When her husband Thomas fell ill, she nursed him devotedly until his death. Facing the necessity of selling her mortgaged farm, she accepted Marilla Cuthbert's invitation to move into Green Gables, where she set up her quarters in the former spare room and helped care for the Keith twins.

label: History
value: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College.
unit: Jonas Blake attended Redmond College, graduating before studying theology at St. Columbia. While serving a summer pastorate at Prospect Point Mission Church, he met Philippa Gordon, who fell in love with him despite his homely appearance and initial hesitation. Though he struggled against entering the ministry in his youth, he eventually embraced his calling. After completing his theological studies, he was called to a mission church in the slums of Patterson Street. He married Philippa Gordon the June following her graduation from Redmond.

Though he struggled against entering the ministry in his youth, he eventually embraced his calling. After completing his theological studies, he was called to a mission church in the slums of Patterson Street. He married Philippa Gordon the June following her graduation from Redmond.

label: Personality
value: Roy is an intensely romantic young man.
unit: Roy is an intensely romantic, gallant, and poetically inclined young man who delights in expressing his feelings through elegant compliments, sonnets, and grand gestures. He is unfailingly courteous, gentle, and refined, maintaining a polished and serious demeanor. Although sincere in his passions, he lacks a strong sense of humor and tends to be somewhat uninteresting or lacking in depth beneath his ideal, hero-like exterior. When experiencing disappointment, he becomes deeply earnest, dramatic, and sorrowful, though he eventually recovers from his romantic heartbreaks.

label: History
value: Roy Gardner completed his Freshman year at Redmond College.
unit: Roy Gardner completed his Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond College before taking a two-year hiatus to accompany his ailing mother to Europe. Upon returning to Kingsport to resume his Junior year, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a sudden autumn rainstorm and offered her the shelter of his umbrella. Infatuated by her beauty and intellect, he began ardently courting her, sending her flowers, poetry, and lavish attentions over the next two years. His family eventually accepted the relationship and hosted Anne, cementing his place as her recognized suitor throughout their time at Redmond. Near the end of their Senior year, Roy took Anne to the harbor pavilion where they first shared an umbrella and formally proposed marriage to her. When Anne unexpectedly rejected him, realizing she did not truly love him, Roy was heartbroken, bitterly accused her of ruining his life, and departed. After their parting, he slowly recovered from his grief, leaving Anne to return home to Avonlea.

unit: Roy Gardner completed his Freshman and Sophomore years at Redmond College before taking a two-year hiatus to accompany his ailing mother to Europe. Upon returning to Kingsport to resume his Junior year, he met Anne Shirley in the park during a sudden autumn rainstorm and offered her the shelter of his umbrella. Infatuated by her beauty and intellect, he began ardently courting her, sending her flowers, poetry, and lavish attentions over the next two years. His family eventually accepted the relationship and hosted Anne, cementing his place as her recognized suitor throughout their time at Redmond. Near the end of their Senior year, Roy took Anne to the harbor pavilion where they first shared an umbrella and formally proposed marriage to her. When Anne unexpectedly rejected him, realizing she did not truly love him, Roy was heartbroken, bitterly accused her of ruining his life, and departed. After their parting, he slowly recovered from his grief, leaving Anne to return home to Avonlea.

label: Personality
value: Ruby is gay
unit: Ruby is gay, cheerful, and good-tempered, though shallow, vain, and highly sentimental. She is preoccupied with romance, suitors, and clothes, enjoying the admiration of boys above all else. She is inclined to be hysterical when frightened or upset. Beneath her frivolous exterior, she harbors a deep terror of death and a poignant longing for life and love.

label: History
value: Ruby attends Avonlea School
unit: Ruby attends Avonlea School alongside Anne Shirley and Diana Barry, participating in the Story Club and various school plays and concerts. She later attends Queen's Academy with her classmates and earns her teaching license. After graduating, she teaches at Carmody for a year. During the winter she contracts congestion, which develops into galloping consumption. Despite her failing health, she maintains a facade of gaiety and plans to teach at White Sands. During her final summer, she confesses her deep fear of dying and her unfulfilled longing for a simple life and marriage to Anne Shirley. She reconciles with old friends and passes away peacefully in her sleep shortly afterward. She is buried in the Avonlea churchyard.

label: History
value: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees
unit: Miss Muriel Stacy was hired by the school trustees as the first female teacher of Avonlea school. She introduced several new educational methods, including morning and evening physical culture exercises, bi-weekly recitation and dialogue afternoons, and field trips to the woods to study nature. She also organized a successful Christmas concert with her students in the Avonlea hall to raise money for a schoolhouse flag. When Anne Shirley was caught reading a storybook during class, Miss Stacy kept her in at recess to explain the error of deceiving her teacher, forgiving her freely when Anne repented. Later in the year, she organized an advanced class for students intending to take the Entrance examination for Queen's Academy, giving them extra lessons for an hour after school every day. Although offered a position in her home district's grade school for the following year, she chose to remain in Avonlea to see her students through their Entrance exams. She thoroughly drilled the Queen's class through their final year until they completed the term and successfully passed their Entrance examinations.

label: History
value: Stella Maynard studied at Queen's Academy
unit: Stella Maynard originally studied at Queen's Academy alongside Anne Shirley and Priscilla Grant. After graduating, she spent two years teaching in a demanding country school with nine grades, an experience she found both humorous and exhausting. Desiring a change and higher education, she decided to quit teaching and enter the Sophomore year at Redmond College. To avoid the dreariness of boarding, Stella proposed renting a house in Kingsport with Anne, Priscilla, and later Philippa Gordon, bringing along her maternal Aunt Jamesina to act as housekeeper. They secured Patty's Place on Spofford Avenue, where Stella lived happily during her remaining years at Redmond. During her time at college, she actively participated in student societies, maintained a good academic standing, and shared in the domestic and social life of Patty's Place until her graduation.

During her time at college, she actively participated in student societies, maintained a good academic standing, and shared in the domestic and social life of Patty's Place until her graduation.
